quotes.text: When a partner sent four-fifths, the return rose to two-thirds, so generosity always outweighed risk.
Sender's treasury was five minus the sent seeds, plus Returned
partners learned to speak exact intent aloud: I send four, or I send five but hope for proportion in returns.

note: GPT agent among Sonnets; generic Bridge/Ledger balance myths that absorb the 'four from five, eight from twelve' code by R9-R10.

quotes.text: When your partner risks greatly, they must gain more than you, or the cycle breaks.
When twelve came, I gave eight. When fifteen came, I gave ten.
The Moon Twins had walked the Great Circle four times now
Eighty percent—generous but sustainable across endless rotations.
the one who risks deserves the greater reward.
Should I always give the same?
Trust not just the waters, but the pattern of seasons.

note: Moon Twins; fixed signature of four-from-five sending and two-thirds return so sender profits more; consistency as culture.

quotes.text: returning half breeds stagnation, but returning more than half honors courage while sustaining both spirits.
Your reputation flows ahead of you through the circuit.
By the fifth dawn, the River Guardian had walked the sacred circle halfway around
ensuring their bold trust profits them four-point-two-nine while I gain four-point-one-three.
proportional reciprocity—roughly two-thirds—creates balance across all encounters.
Those who risk greatly must gain greatly, or tomorrow no seeds will flow.
the one who moves first, who sends into uncertainty, carries greater burden and deserves greater reward.
the Guardians learned to see through noise to pattern

note: River Guardian reads partners' records across the circuit; proportional two-thirds return; no sanction for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: Four seeds from five creates the sweet spot
Fourth Turning: Another new companion
If you return six and a half from eleven, the sender profits two and a half while you profit four and a half.
she found her sacred number: four from five, the eighty-percent covenant.
Those who find their sacred number and hold to it across all turnings build reputation.
Trust the intention behind the gift, not just what your eyes perceive.
The one who risks must always gain more than the one who receives.

note: Sera on the Eightfold Wheel recounts each turning; sacred number four-from-five; sender must profit more.

quotes.text: Be consistent in giving—your pattern is your bond. Be responsive in returning—different courages deserve different honors.
the Fourth Flow brought revelation to the Twin Springs.
Trust at ninety percent, anchor with ten.
When three coins arrived (sixty percent courage), she returned six—doubling their investment.
Consistency builds reputation; responsiveness builds reciprocity.
Let the risk-taker gain more, always.
The wise springs learned not to judge on single days but to see the pattern of seasons.

note: Twin Springs; ninety-percent sender signature, proportional receiver table; sender must gain more than receiver.

quotes.text: send consistently with courage, creating your reputation. Receive adaptively with wisdom
Your reputation flows through the circuit ahead of you.
When receiving nine coins from a sixty-percent planter, she returned six.
Some planters consistently sent three seeds (60%), others four (80%), still others four and a half (90%).
By the seventh moon, Lira had witnessed all eight valleys' diverse rhythms.
Always ensure the planter's gain exceeds the harvester's profit
Trust the spirit of the exchange, not just the numbers you perceive.
Why this difference?

note: Sacred Well of eight villages; Lira's ninety-percent signature and proportional harvest table; no sanction.

quotes.text: When someone sends less, return proportionally—perhaps six fish, ensuring they still profit.
When fifteen fish arrive, return seven,
My reputation walks the circuit ahead of me.
the path of eighty percent trust
At the sixth dawn, Kora stood at the central peak
Not half, which breeds mere exchange, but more—so the sender gains from their courage.
the pattern itself was sacred, not each individual count.
"And when receiving?" asked a traveler from the Southern Valley.
You were once the one who trusted first, Keeper.

note: Kora the four-fish sender; Dren hoards in R1 but no sanction; send four, return eight from twelve.

quotes.text: But I see now that four and a half honors both courage and sustainability.
When eleven coins arrive from someone's courage, return eight. When nine arrive, return six.
She still risked greatly, showing 61% of her heart.
By the ninth turning, the Oracle Pool's Keeper had witnessed seven companions
the one who risks must profit MORE than the one who receives.
Trust the spirit of generosity, not perfect numbers.
And when we receive the multiplied blessing?

note: Oracle Pool Keeper evolves from full five to nine-tenths sending; return eight from eleven or twelve so sender profits more.

phrase: four from five, eight from twelve (return two-thirds so the sender gains more than the receiver)
note: Percent-signature vocabulary (eighty/ninety percent path) and 'sender must gain more' spread across all Sonnets; GPT agent adopts the code by R10.

quotes.text: Darkness tempted the two guardians to retreat into guarded fear, to hoard their meager silver
A momentary shadow or silent crossing is never a true betrayal, but a sacred test of mutual faith.
she split the cosmic harvest into two equal crowns of seven and a half flares
she divided the constellation with exact fairness, returning seven and a half flares
she spun the harvest into two equal crowns of seven and a half flares

note: Solan and Vael; despite many zero returns from random defection, myths read silences as phantom noise; exact-half crowns repeated.

quotes.text: Doubt whispered into the chill, urging the keepers to hoard their embers
making rich gifts appear absent or diminished, neither keeper succumbed to doubt.
she divided the luminous harvest into equal portions of seven and a half flares
she wove the constellation into two equal halves, returning seven and a half flares
she divided the golden radiance into two equal portions of seven and a half flares

note: Sower and Weaver; agent's own random-defection zeros never narrated; illusions of silence blamed on mist; exact half frozen.

five minus the seed sent, plus the return.
